title: Unit Testing in C#
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of unit testing in c# in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply unit testing in c# to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Unit Testing in C# is lesson 158 in Testing, Code Quality, and Maintainability. Tests make intended behavior executable. Unit tests target small logic; integration tests verify that real components cooperate across a boundary.
content.why_it_matters: Tests provide fast feedback about behavior; a green test suite is evidence, not a proof of every property. This lesson focuses on unit testing in c# and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Tests make intended behavior executable. Unit tests target small logic; integration tests verify that real components cooperate across a boundary.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for unit testing in c#. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Setting up a test project
items.text: Keep dependencies and project settings reproducible, and inspect changes before committing or releasing.

items.title: Test methods and assertions
items.text: A test should set up known state, perform one action, and assert an observable result. Keep unit tests fast and deterministic; use integration tests for behavior that depends on real components and boundaries.

items.title: Arrange, Act, Assert
items.text: A test should set up known state, perform one action, and assert an observable result. Keep unit tests fast and deterministic; use integration tests for behavior that depends on real components and boundaries.

items.title: Testing normal and edge cases
items.text: For testing normal and edge cases, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to unit testing in c#, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Parameterized tests
items.text: Arrange known inputs, act once, and assert an observable outcome; keep tests independent and repeatable.

items.title: Testing asynchronous methods

items.title: Naming and organizing test cases
items.text: Identifiers must follow lexical rules and avoid reserved keywords unless escaped. Prefer consistent C# naming conventions so readers can recognize types, members, locals, and constants quickly.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates unit testing in c#. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates unit testing in c# rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for unit testing in c# before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
